newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Skala to boost stake in Centrum to 37pct.
newsitem.headline: Skala to boost stake in Centrum to 37pct.

text.p: Skala-Coop Rt, the Hungarian unit of Germany's Tengelmann, will boost its stake in its competitor, retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt, to some 37 percent from 25 percent, Skala-Coop said on Monday.
"We will raise Centrum's capital by one billion forints (to some six billion forints)," Skala-Coop Chairman Istvan Imre told Reuters. "Our stake will increase to 37 percent."
"We decided that for the short term we will be minority owners," he said.
He added that Skala-Coop would examine if further investments in Centrum would provide sufficient returns.
"Who invests almost 40 percent in a company, obviously cannot be regarded as a simple financial investor," he said.

An extraordinary shareholders meeting of Centrum on Sunday approved the capital increase by Skala-Coop, and Skala-Coop was likely to delegate managers to Centrum at the annual meeting of Centrum's shareholders, to help a restructuring of Centrum.
Imre said Centrum needs to carry out investments of several billions of forints, but a substantial part of the funds should be raised by Centrum itself.
Centrum operates 25 supermarkets, nine of them in the capital Budapest, the daily Vilaggazdasag said.
Skala was trading at 2,270 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange at 1003 GMT, up by 210 forints.
